capabilities: Edit Markdown tables in an infinite spreadsheet grid with Excel-like keys and a formula bar
Calculate formulas stored inside cells as Obsidian comments, with cross-table references
Sort, filter, split, merge and clean table data, and pivot tables read-only
Import CSV, TSV and Excel files and export tables to CSV, Excel, JSON or formatted text
Merge external files into a table by a key column
extras: States explicit limits: tables up to about 500 rows (grid stops at 2000 rows and 128 columns), no support for tables inside callouts or block quotes, and mobile touch layout not yet tested on every device. Makes no network requests and has no runtime dependencies. Manual review status noted in the manifest.
problem: Obsidian has no spreadsheet-like way to edit Markdown tables; editing them cell by cell in raw text is slow and error-prone.
